question.text: In computing data for performance benchmarking, SEBI's operational guidelines specify the basis of reporting for Cat III AIF returns. Which of the following is correct?

answer.text: Post-tax NAV; AUM equals committed capital
Pre-tax NAV; AUM equals value of total capital drawn down under the scheme
Post-expense, post-carry, post-tax NAV; AUM equals NAV of the scheme
Gross-of-fees NAV; AUM equals Gross Asset Value including leverage

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI operational guidelines (Box 8.6, Section A): 'AUM for the purpose of reporting and benchmarking shall be the value of total capital drawn down under the Scheme. Performance reporting and benchmarking shall be carried out on pre-tax Net Asset Value (NAV) of the Scheme.' For Cat III specifically, returns are reported post-expense, pre-carry, pre-tax. The Trap: Option A swaps the rules (post-tax and committed capital). Option C adds carry deduction and post-tax NAV — inconsistent with the SEBI basis. Option D uses GAV, which overstates the base due to Cat III leverage. Note: Cat III is taxed at fund level, so pre-tax NAV is the consistent reporting basis used by the benchmarking agency.
